items.title: John Batiste "Bat" Stecklet Interview, 1959-06-15
items.q: [INTERVIEWEE] No I don't remember him either.

ctx.x: Well, you see, the violin players rule, most all of them that I know that I used to play with, they used to play the melody, you understand, just the same as mostly I would. But they learned all that from me, you see. And that was why every time they'd get a job, they'd come, sometimes they'd be three or four fellas that'd come from me for the play the same night that I had already been engaged. You understand? Yes. Well, the reason they'd done it is just like lances and varieties. Them fellas couldn't play no…

Yeah. I was wondering about Gala Nunez. Do you remember about how old he was? Was he older than you? Well, he was a much younger man than I was. Well, he's younger than you. Now, do you know what part of town he came from? Since he's not here, we'll never be able to talk to him and find out. He was a whole

lot younger man than I was. I couldn't tell you his age, but I do know that he was a much younger man than I was. Did he come from about the same part of town, downtown here? Yes. Well, I know somewhere between the Leeson Field and, say, El Manasio over here. Well, what they call it now, they changed the name to Franklin Avenue. Franklin Avenue. Franklin Avenue. And then it runs back from the, way up from the beginning near the river to back here where the, where Franklin Avenue turns off this way. Yeah. And the…
